stops.note: literally tradition or received knowledge, referring to Jewish mystical teaching
broadened in French to mean any secret intrigue or scheme
Charles II's ministry of 1667–73 was nicknamed the 'Cabal' because its members' initials (Clifford, Arlington, Buckingham, Ashley, Lauderdale) spelled the word
stops.meaning: a secret political faction or conspiracy

current_meaning: a secret group of people plotting together, especially in politics
